title: The Kalopaideia German Examination
instructions: Three hours, no notes for Part A; printed lexicon and grammar permitted for Part B. Honor code: you affirm by submitting that you used only permitted aids. A failed examination may be retaken after thirty days.

items.prompt_german: Sagt es niemand, nur den Weisen, / Weil die Menge gleich verhöhnet.
items.prompt_en: Translate this opening couplet from Goethe's 'Selige Sehnsucht' (West-östlicher Divan).
reference: Tell it to no one, only to the wise, / For the crowd will mock at once
Tell no one, only the wise, / Because the crowd mocks immediately
Say it to no one, only to the wise, / For the multitude will ridicule it

items.prompt_german: Wer reitet so spät durch Nacht und Wind? / Es ist der Vater mit seinem Kind.
items.prompt_en: Translate this opening couplet from Goethe's 'Erlkönig'.
reference: Who rides so late through night and wind? / It is the father with his child
Who rides so late through night and wind? / It's the father with his child
Who is riding so late through night and wind? / It is the father with his child

items.prompt_german: Als Zarathustra dreißig Jahre alt war, verließ er seine Heimat und den See seiner Heimat und ging in das Gebirge.
items.prompt_en: Translate this opening sentence of Nietzsche's 'Also sprach Zarathustra', Vorrede §1.
reference: When Zarathustra was thirty years old, he left his home and the lake of his home and went into the mountains
When Zarathustra turned thirty, he left his homeland and the lake of his homeland and went to the mountains
As Zarathustra was thirty years old, he left his home and the lake of his home and went into the mountains

items.prompt_german: Gott ist tot! Gott bleibt tot! Und wir haben ihn getötet!
items.prompt_en: Translate this famous line from Nietzsche.
reference: God is dead! God remains dead! And we have killed him!
God is dead! God stays dead! And we have killed him!
God is dead! God is still dead! And we killed him!

items.prompt_german: Als Gregor Samsa eines Morgens aus unruhigen Träumen erwachte, fand er sich in seinem Bett zu einem ungeheueren Ungeziefer verwandelt.
items.prompt_en: Translate this opening sentence of Kafka's 'Die Verwandlung'.
reference: When Gregor Samsa woke one morning from uneasy dreams, he found himself transformed in his bed into a monstrous vermin
As Gregor Samsa awoke one morning from troubled dreams, he found himself transformed in his bed into a gigantic insect
When Gregor Samsa woke up one morning from restless dreams, he found himself in his bed transformed into a huge bug

items.prompt_en: Translate Gregor's first thought after his transformation.
reference: What has happened to me?
What happened to me?
What has become of me?

items.prompt: Parse the form *sagte*. Give: person, number, tense, mood, voice, infinitive.
Parse the form *hätte*. Give: person, number, tense, mood, voice, infinitive.
Parse the noun form *des Mannes*. Give: case, number, gender, nominative singular.
Parse the form *wurde*. Give: person, number, tense, mood, voice, infinitive.
Parse the adjective *guten* in the phrase *den guten Mann*. Give: case, number, gender, declension type (strong/weak/mixed).
Render in German: 'The man is old.'
reference: Der Mann ist alt
Der Mann ist alt.

items.prompt: Render in German: 'I see the book.'
reference: Ich sehe das Buch
Ich sehe das Buch.

items.prompt: Render in German: 'The woman gives the child a book.'
reference: Die Frau gibt dem Kind ein Buch
Die Frau gibt dem Kind ein Buch.
Die Frau gibt ein Buch dem Kind

items.prompt: Render in German: 'If I had time, I would come.'
reference: Wenn ich Zeit hätte, würde ich kommen
Wenn ich Zeit hätte, würde ich kommen.
Wenn ich Zeit hätte, käme ich

items.prompt: Render in German: 'The book was read by the student.' (passive voice)
reference: Das Buch wurde vom Studenten gelesen
Das Buch wurde vom Studenten gelesen.
Das Buch wurde von dem Studenten gelesen

sections.title: Part D — Multiple Choice (vocabulary and idiom)

items.prompt: What case does the preposition *mit* govern?
Which auxiliary verb does *gehen* take in the present perfect?
What is the Konjunktiv II form of *sein* for the first-person singular?
In a two-way preposition phrase, which case indicates motion toward a place?
What does *Ungeziefer* mean (Kafka's word for Gregor's new form)?
What is the past participle of *lesen*?
